title: VRCX-K Plugin Manifest
description: Author-owned plugin declaration, read from <plugin-root>/.vrcxk/manifest.json. AUTHORITATIVE for version, dependencies, services and permissions. The marketplace index carries only a display cache of name/description; everything else is read from this file. See docs/plugin-source-and-index-design.md.

$schema.description: Editor-only pointer for autocomplete/validation. IGNORED at load time (Claude Code precedent).

id.description: Stable plugin identifier. MUST match the id of the marketplace index entry that references this plugin.

version.description: Authoritative semantic version. MUST equal the version segment of the release tag that points at this commit (tag `v1.2.0` or `{id}--v1.2.0`). Checked when installing that ONE version (O(1)), never per-tag.

author.description: Required. Part of the identity tuple used to DETECT a change of owner (id + version + author). It is a change detector, not an authenticator: it is self-declared, and differences are reported to the user without blocking (design P2).

name.description: Display name. Authoritative; the index copy is only a cache.

repository.description: Source repository. Doubles as an identity signal: if it changes for the same id, the user is told.

platforms.description: Operating systems on which this plugin's NATIVE part can load. Omit for pure JS/TS (the default, and the common case) — a pure JS plugin is platform-independent. Pair with `arch` when the plugin bundles native code: the two fields together are what make an x64-only library correctly REJECTED on arm64 rather than installed and then failing at load. This says nothing about clients: the phone runs no host, hence no plugin (docs/mobile-feasibility.md).

arch.description: CPU architectures the plugin's native part supports. Only meaningful alongside `platforms`; omitting it means every architecture of those platforms. Required in practice for any plugin shipping a native library, because architecture is exactly the axis a single `platforms` value cannot express.

restartClass.description: How a CHANGE to this plugin takes effect. Not a category label: without it the host would restart the whole sidecar even for a UI-only plugin. The two non-default values impose DUTIES on the author (see each description).

dependencies.description: Plugin dependencies, npm model: a map of plugin id -> version range. NEVER names a source — the author cannot know which sources the user has configured. Sources resolve at install time from the user's current priority list.

services.description: Service readiness and provision. `required` is a READINESS GATE and is the authority from which the host derives the cordis Entry `inject` (single direction, no drift).

permissions.description: Capability declaration for transparency: shown at install time and used for over-privilege WARNINGS. Never enforced (design P2; module-level interception is explicitly not promised).

frontend.description: Frontend extension point (M3). Omit for headless plugins.

SemVer.description: semver.org, verbatim regex. Prerelease identifiers admit only [0-9A-Za-z-]: an underscore is NOT legal semver, which is why the tag suffix charset excludes it (giving it up would mean writing our own comparator). Note prereleases sort BEFORE the release (1.2.0-rc < 1.2.0) and are excluded from ranges unless explicitly opted in. Our convention additionally caps the prerelease at 24 characters — enforced by the validator, not by this pattern, since it is a house rule rather than a spec rule.

VersionRange.description: A semver range, e.g. *, ^1.2, ~2.1.0, >=1.4 <2, =2.1.0. Prereleases are excluded unless the range opts in (^2.0.0-0).

Platform.description: Operating system only, and deliberately coarse: the ARCHITECTURE is a separate axis (`arch`). A single `windows` value cannot distinguish x64 from arm64, so an x64-only native library would be judged compatible on arm64 — the two fields together express what six combined values would, without a value that mixes the axes.

Arch.description: CPU architecture. These are OUR names rather than `process.arch` values, so the schema does not inherit a Node rename; the host maps them when checking.

RestartClass.description: restartable (default): sidecar restart + auto-reconnect; no author duty. frontend: entry broadcast + WebView reload, no backend restart; the author must make frontend assets independently reloadable. background: plugin-level refresh on config change and rolling replacement on upgrade; the author MUST implement a refresh contract plus reconnect and state recovery. v0 accepts ONLY `restartable` and rejects the others (an error, never a silent downgrade); M3 opens `frontend`, M4 opens `background`. The schema already carries the full vocabulary so it need not change — only the accepted subset widens.

DependencyKey.description: A plugin id (kebab-case, e.g. `base-storage`) OR a service name (camelCase, e.g. `storage`). Both spellings are accepted TODAY, and that is deliberate: naming a SERVICE is what makes an implementation swappable, because a dependency on a service is satisfied by whoever provides it rather than by one specific plugin. Resolving a service-named dependency is not implemented yet (v0 resolves plugin ids); accepting the spelling now means adding third-party implementations later will not require editing every existing manifest. See docs/plugin-source-and-index-design.md §3.6.

ServiceName.description: Service identity: a context key (`notify`) or a provisioned service name (`friendPresence`). Names that LEAK AN IMPLEMENTATION are rejected: a trailing `Impl`/`Implementation` (e.g. `storageImpl`) or a first-party prefix (`baseStorage`, `officialStorage`). This is the swap-ability guard — a dependency on `storage` can be satisfied by any provider, whereas `baseStorage` bakes one implementation into every dependent's manifest and makes a third-party replacement impossible without editing them all. Must start lowercase so a camelCase service name can never be confused with a kebab-case plugin id.

required.description: Readiness gate: the plugin is not started until these are provided. The host derives the cordis Entry `inject` from this list.

optional.description: Used when present; the plugin degrades gracefully when absent.

implements.description: Services this plugin PROVIDES. Currently display-only metadata (no dependency resolution consumes it yet); retained because removing it later would be a schema change. Declaring it is what makes a 'library' plugin visible as such.

oneOf.description: true = request the whole domain (coarse grant, permitted).
A narrow grant: specific methods, or (for shell) sub-domains.

ShellSubdomain.description: ctx.shell is the raw escape hatch and can only be granted at SUB-DOMAIN granularity — method-level narrowing is not implementable for it. Keys mirror RAW_SHELL in host/src/capability.ts.

HandsPrimitive.description: The file primitives ctx.hands can be granted at, one entry per primitive. PRIMITIVE granularity, not a single boolean and not a path scope: hands is a sharper permission than ctx.shell because it reaches the whole disk, so 'read and stat, never write' must be expressible. Path-scoped grants are deliberately not modelled yet — they need a matcher both sides honour, and the enforcement layer is #13/M4. Keys mirror HANDS_PRIMITIVES in host/src/contracts/capabilityInventory.ts. `list` enumerates ONE directory (non-recursive, unfiltered); matching, sorting and recursion are caller policy, but enumeration ITSELF is a capability only the shell can perform for a remote node.

Permissions.description: Minimal privilege is ENCOURAGED, not enforced: a plugin may request a whole domain or list narrow entries. The key set is the runtime capability inventory; a contract test pins it to what the host actually provides so the two cannot drift.

shell.description: Raw shell surface. Sub-domain granularity only. ⚠ `maxItems` MUST equal the `ShellSubdomain` enum length, or a plugin granting every sub-domain has its whole manifest rejected — which silently disables the `#24` warn for exactly the most-privileged plugins. A contract test pins the two together.

autostart.description: Register the app to start with the system. Desktop only; the shell registers no such route on mobile.

oneOf.description: A narrow grant: exactly the listed primitives.

hands.description: File primitives (stat/read/write/watch/list). Reaches the whole disk, so prefer a narrow list over `true`. Declaration only at this stage — not enforced (#24 is declare-and-warn, and the real boundary is M4's subprocess isolation). ⚠ `maxItems` MUST equal the `HandsPrimitive` enum length: adding a primitive to the enum without raising this made a 5-primitive grant INVALID, so the manifest was rejected and the `#24` warn silently switched off. A contract test pins the two together.

entry.description: Path to the frontend entry, RELATIVE to the plugin root. Must not escape it: a `..` segment anywhere (including a trailing one, e.g. `ui/..`) is rejected, as is a leading `/`. Note a path regex cannot catch percent-encoding or Windows drive/UNC forms — the loader resolves the path and re-checks containment, which is what actually enforces this.

slots.description: Extension points this plugin registers into. The vocabulary lands with the M3 frontend contract.
